record.context_brief: Recognizing hypergraphs of induced directed cycles
record.original_question: Given a 3-uniform hypergraph H, decide whether there exists a digraph D such that the hypergraph H_D on V(D), whose hyperedges are exactly the induced directed cycles of D, is equal to H.

evidence.quote: From a digraph D = (V,A), build the hypergraph HD on V whose hyperedges are the induced directed cycles of D.
Given a (3-uniform) hypergraph H , decide if there exist D such that HD = H .

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a digraph D = (V, A) (a directed graph without loops or multiple arcs), define the 3-uniform hypergraph H_D as follows: the vertex set of H_D is V, and the hyperedges of H_D are exactly the vertex sets {x, y, z} ⊆ V such that x, y, z induce a directed 3-cycle in D (i.e., up to relabeling, (x,y), (y,z), (z,x) ∈ A and no other arcs are present among {x, y, z}).

Determine the computational complexity of the following decision problem: given a 3-uniform hypergraph H, decide whether there exists a digraph D with V(D) = V(H) such that H_D = H. In particular, give an algorithm that decides this problem, or show that the problem is NP-hard.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not return any source explicitly resolving the recognition problem for 3-uniform hypergraphs arising as the set of induced directed 3-cycles of a digraph. No algorithm or hardness proof for this specific problem was located, so the current status is unclear from publicly available results.

status_evidence.title: Threshold Digraphs (PMC)
status_evidence.snippet: An induced directed 3-cycle is a set of three vertices x, y, z so that (x, y), (y, z), (z, x) are arcs but there are no other arcs among the vertices.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms standard definition of induced directed 3-cycle relevant to the problem, but does not address the recognition problem.

status_evidence.title: Directed hypergraphs: A tool for researching digraphs and hypergraphs
status_evidence.snippet: Directed hypergraphs are a generalization of digraphs and are closely related with hypergraphs.
status_evidence.claim: General context only; the specific recognition problem is not addressed.
